title: The Flight Instructors
eyebrow: Case file · regression to the mean
lede: Our worst region got a new manager and improved. Did the manager work? A hundred pilots, two days of landings, and nobody saying a word.

commit.title: YOUR NUMBER
commit.prompt: Of today's 10 best landings, how many land worse tomorrow? Nobody praises or shouts.

captions: Your worst region got a new manager.
Next quarter it climbed. So the manager worked?
Before the case, commit to a number.
Flight instructors: praise a great landing, next is worse.
Scream at a bad one, the next is better. So shouting works?
Kahneman: a landing is skill plus luck. Luck is redrawn.
Best: 83 = skill 65 + luck 18. Next day, luck −6: 59.
Tomorrow: same pilots. No praise. No shouting.
8 of the top 10 land worse. Nobody said a word.
Your guess, on the rail. The count says 8.
Bottom 10: 8 of 10 land better. Both ends drift halfway.
Monday: what did the worst regions do with no fix?
Limit: the manager may help. One quarter can't show it.

brand.takeaway: The extremes drift back on their own. Credit needs a comparison.

sources: Tversky A, Kahneman D. Judgment under uncertainty: heuristics and biases. Science 1974;185(4157):1124-1131. doi:10.1126/science.185.4157.1124. The flight-training anecdote.
Kahneman D. Thinking, Fast and Slow. New York: Farrar, Straus and Giroux; 2011. Chapter 17, Regression to the Mean.
Galton F. Regression towards mediocrity in hereditary stature. Journal of the Anthropological Institute 1886;15:246-263. doi:10.2307/2841583.
Secrist H. The Triumph of Mediocrity in Business. Evanston, IL: Northwestern University Bureau of Business Research; 1933. With Hotelling H., letter, JASA 1934;29(186):198-199.
Barnett AG, van der Pols JC, Dobson AJ. Regression to the mean: what it is and how to deal with it. Int J Epidemiol 2005;34(1):215-220. doi:10.1093/ije/dyh299.

Declared teaching model: landing = skill + luck, mean 50, SD 10, skill and luck equally variable (r = 0.5); 100 pilots from rounded normal quantiles, luck shuffled by mulberry32 (seeds 1468 and 2468).
honest: The hundred pilots are a constructed sample from a declared model, not flight-school data. The instructors' story is an anecdote that carries no numbers of its own.

r = 0.5 is a choice: skill and luck made equally variable. Real measures have their own r; Galton's heights (928 adult children of 205 parent couples, 1886) kept about two-thirds of the parents' distance from average.

Seed 1468 was the only one of 5,000 scanned whose counts sit at the model's expected values (8.4 of 10 worse, 3.2 stay top 10) with no ties at the cuts: a typical sample, picked to be typical. Sample r is 0.49.
This does not say feedback or the manager does nothing. It says a before-and-after on a unit picked for being extreme cannot measure it; a comparison group picked the same way can.

tryit.title: Try it
tryit.note: Change r, the share of the gap that is skill. The model lines follow; the drawn sample does not.
